summary: For OpenShift Virtualization, build the Edge Manager bootc image with late binding via cloud-init, add open-vm-tools, and produce a qcow2 disk image instead of an iso. The Containerfile installs flightctl-agent, cloud-init and open-vm-tools; podman-compose can optionally be added from EPEL.
questions: How do I build an Edge Manager image for OpenShift Virtualization?
What Containerfile installs flightctl-agent and cloud-init?
Why use qcow2 instead of iso for OpenShift Virtualization?
How do I add podman-compose support to a bootc image?

answer_card.title: Bootc image for OpenShift Virtualization
answer_card.answer_md:
Differences from the generic build:
- Late binding: inject enrollment config via **cloud-init** at provisioning
- Add `open-vm-tools`
- Disk image type `qcow2`, not `iso`

```dockerfile
FROM registry.redhat.io/rhel9/bootc-image-builder:latest
RUN subscription-manager repos --enable ansible-automation-platform-2.5-for-rhel-9-x86_64-rpms && \
    dnf -y install flightctl-agent && dnf -y clean all && \
    systemctl enable flightctl-agent.service
RUN dnf -y install cloud-init open-vm-tools && dnf -y clean all && \
    ln -s ../cloud-init.target /usr/lib/systemd/system/default.target.wants && \
    systemctl enable vmtoolsd.service
```
